name: Olaparib
route_note: oral tablets twice daily (capsule formulation discontinued)
originator: KuDOS Pharmaceuticals (Cambridge, UK; Stephen Jackson); developed by AstraZeneca

discovery.by: KuDOS Pharmaceuticals; synthetic lethality with BRCA shown by Alan Ashworth's and Thomas Helleday's groups
discovery.note: A phthalazinone PARP inhibitor; AstraZeneca acquired KuDOS in 2005.

tagline: First PARP inhibitor, exploiting synthetic lethality in BRCA-mutated cancers
summary: Olaparib is an oral PARP inhibitor that kills cancer cells unable to repair DNA by homologous recombination, notably those with BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations — a concept known as synthetic lethality. It is approved for ovarian, breast, pancreatic and prostate cancers, including as maintenance and adjuvant therapy.
mechanism: PARP1 and PARP2 detect single-strand DNA breaks and recruit repair factors. Olaparib inhibits PARP catalytic activity and traps PARP on DNA, so unrepaired lesions and trapped complexes are converted into double-strand breaks when replication forks collide with them.

Normal cells repair these breaks by homologous recombination, but cells lacking BRCA1, BRCA2 or other homologous-recombination genes cannot, and they die — synthetic lethality. Reversion mutations restoring BRCA function are a common cause of resistance.
uses: Maintenance treatment of advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer (BRCA-mutated first-line, with bevacizumab in HRD-positive disease, or platinum-sensitive relapse)
Adjuvant treatment of germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer
Germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer
Maintenance in germline BRCA-mutated metastatic pancreatic cancer
HRR gene-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (alone or with abiraterone)

history.title: Synthetic lethality
history.detail: Bryant et al. and Farmer et al. (Nature) show BRCA-deficient cells are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibition; AstraZeneca acquires KuDOS.

history.title: Phase I
history.detail: Fong et al. (NEJM) report responses in BRCA mutation carriers.

history.title: First approvals
history.detail: EMA (December 16) and FDA (December 19) approve olaparib capsules for BRCA-mutated ovarian cancer.

history.title: Tablets and Merck deal
history.detail: Tablet formulation approved; AstraZeneca and Merck form a global collaboration.

history.title: Breast cancer and SOLO-1
history.detail: Approvals for gBRCA metastatic breast cancer (OlympiAD) and first-line ovarian maintenance.

history.title: Pancreatic cancer
history.detail: POLO leads to approval for gBRCA metastatic pancreatic cancer maintenance.

history.title: Prostate cancer
history.detail: PROfound leads to approval in HRR-mutated mCRPC.

history.title: Adjuvant breast cancer
history.detail: OlympiA leads to adjuvant approval in high-risk gBRCA early breast cancer.

serious: myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukaemia

facts: Olaparib was the first approved drug based on the principle of synthetic lethality.
